messages:
leo: quick heads-up — rolled ptq-litev3:canary to streaming yesterday. seeing a concentrated spike in structured-output parse errors tied to multibyte UTF-8 sequences being split across stream chunks. error: `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x82 in position 234`

anya: streaming-only? any raw chunks we can look at?

leo: yes. mirror slice shows chunk boundary splitting a 3-byte UTF-8 sequence (example uses euro sign U+20AC). raw (proxy hex-escaped for safety):
```
chunk A: {"delta":"...\xE2\x82","finish_reason":null}
chunk B: {"delta":"\xAC...","finish_reason":"stop"}
```
coalescing as text currently produces literal "...\\xE2\\x82\\xAC..." or sometimes leaves a broken binary byte which the JSON parser chokes on depending on transport escaping.

maria: interesting — tokenizer shouldn't emit half codepoints, but streaming chunker can split at arbitrary byte boundaries when we splice kvcache frames + new tokens. quantization might change token lengths and therefore where we cut.

devon: eval-bot, what's the telemetry?

eval-bot: parse_error_rate(ptq-litev3:canary)=0.018 over last 4h. baseline(raven-v2-q8)=0.0005. top affected endpoints: tool-invoke, file-parser. Majority of failures correlate with high-batch/kv-prefix hits.

anya: hypothesis: kvcache stores prefix frames as raw bytes; streamer naively concatenates text chunks without guarding UTF-8 boundaries. quantized model output distribution shifted tokenization so more multi-byte codepoints now end up at chunk ends.

leo: mitigation suggestions: 1) make streamer UTF-8 boundary aware — never emit a text chunk that ends in an incomplete UTF-8 lead byte; hold trailing bytes until next frame, 2) as temporary workaround, base64-encode any binary prefix frames so proxy treats them as opaque text, 3) add sanitizer to try "replace" or "surrogateescape" decode on coalesced stream and log original bytes for forensics.

maria: prefer (1) as long-term. (2) is lower-risk short-term for canary. (3) ok for replay diagnostic. we should also check whether gzip/chunking or proxy double-escaping is worsening this.

devon: plan: a) flip base64-on-prefix for canary at T+5m, b) run 2k replay on failing traces with UTF8-safe coalescer, c) collect hex-dumps for 1% of requests. if replay drops parse errors by >90% we consider rolling base64 to prod as stopgap while we implement proper UTF-8 boundary logic.

leo: filed INF-4410 with samples and request ids. enabling base64-on-prefix at 1849994390. kicking off replay now. ETA ~30m.

anya: small note — for the UTF-8 boundary patch, take care with multi-byte sequences when theres also JSON escaping (e.g., sequences like "\u20AC" vs raw bytes). encoder must operate on bytes before JSON escaping.

eval-bot: update after base64 flip: parse_error_rate(canary, smoke slice)=0.002 in first 10m (down ~89%). full replay results pending.

devon: good signal. if base64 reduces errors significantly, roll to prod for a few hours while runtime patch is developed. make sure this doesn't inflate token counts in observability parsing.

maria: replay finished at 1849994721: UTF8-safe coalescer + base64-on-prefix reduced failures by 93% on the failing cohort. attached hex-dumps to INF-4410. moving to implement the boundary-aware streamer in runtime repo; will TODO a small RFC for the encoder/escaping order. :thumbsup:
